full_judgment: 3. After knowing the fact, one Abdul Jalil Majhi (third party) and others filed an application before the Court of learned District Judge, Barishal under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the said forgery in the plaint and decree of the aforesaid suit. The learned Judge, who after hearing the matter started an inquiry Case No.02 of 1988 and the notice was served upon both parties and after inquiry the learned Subordinate Judge upon hearing all concerned parties and perusing the record, detected the forgery i.e. that in the plaint, suit valuation of the property was shown as TK. 1,25,000/- and the area of the land was shown as 247.88 decimals, and by interpolation, the figure '1' was inserted at the valuation statement of the suit property as well as the quantum of the land and thereby valuation of the suit property was increased to TK.11,25,000/- and the area of the suit was enhanced to 1247.88 decimals. This forgery was committed in schedule Nos.9, 25, 36, 47 and 48 of the plaint as well as in the ex-parte decree. The Court corrected the same on 27.11.1989 vide order No.88. Against the said order of correction, one Md. Yousuf as a third party filed Civil Revision No.547 of 1990 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing was discharged on 13.07.1994. Against the said judgment and order, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.764 of 1994 was filed before this Division and was dismissed on 02.05.1995, thereby upholding the correction made by the trial Court vide order No.88 dated 27.11.1989.
